newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Peron "daughter" wants ex Argentine chief exhumed.
newsitem.headline: Peron "daughter" wants ex Argentine chief exhumed.

text.p: An Argentine woman who wants to prove she is the late President Juan Peron's illegitimate daughter with a DNA test accused his widow on Wednesday of "systematically obstructing" the court case.

"If they want war, they've got it," Martha Holgado, 62, told reporters on the steps of the Buenos Aires Civil Appeals Court. The lawyer of Maria Estela Martinez, Peron's third wife known as Isabel, failed to appear at a hearing to set a date for his exhumation.
Isabel Peron, who became president when he died in office in 1974 but was toppled by a military coup in 1976, does not want his tomb in Buenos Aires' La Chacarita cemetery opened.
"They are systematically delaying things," Holgado said. "But if I am not telling the truth everyone will find out when the test is done."

Now resident in Madrid, like Isabel Peron, Holgado arrived in Buenos Aires in September after winning an appeal to open the tomb of the man who ruled Argentina from 1946-55 and 1973-74 to test his DNA, or genetic material, against hers.

Holgado, who bears a clear resemblance to Peron, says her mother and Peron were lovers in 1932 but that she did not learn she was his daughter until she was 19 and never told anyone because of a pact of secrecy with her mother.

Asked whether she planned to claim Peron's inheritance -- rumoured to include secret Swiss bank accounts -- she said if she is proved to be his daughter she would claim her birthright. Her attorney, Eduardo Barcesat, said another hearing should be convened by the end of the year.
